title: Why we procrastinate
paragraphs: Is your house at its tidiest when you've got a deadline coming up? Do you have a list of jobs that you really need to do, but you really don't want to start doing? Procrastination can mean that we spend more time putting off a job than we'd ever actually spend completing it. Understanding why we do it might help us to understand how to stop doing it.

There are different reasons why people procrastinate. Some people avoid tasks if they can relate them to traumatic situations in their past. Sometimes we don't do certain tasks because we're swamped with other things. If people are unhappy about being asked to do something, they might put it off to feel like they are regaining some control. Another common reason for procrastination is just the worry that doing something will be unpleasant or that we will not be able to do it well enough to satisfy ourselves.

This last kind of procrastination can be a result of our mindset. People with a perfectionist mindset are likely to have a very rigid idea of what success in a task looks like. This is coupled with being anxious not to fail at that task. Psychology lecturer Annemiecke Apergis-Schoute points out that procrastination can be the result of a struggle between our brain's reward and threat systems. If the threat of failure or discomfort is greater than the potential reward from doing the task, we're likely to avoid it.

Cognitive flexibility could help us to avoid procrastinating. If we change the way that we think about a task, it can be easier to start working on it. If we can challenge our expectation of what succeeding could be, and how uncomfortable working on the task will be, it can seem less threatening. Breaking down tasks into small components also makes them less daunting as well as providing a feeling of achievement when each of these steps is completed. It can also be useful to consider what triggers procrastination for you. Having a better understanding of this can help you get things done.
chineseParagraphs: 当截止日期临近时，你的房子是不是变得最整洁？你是否有一堆真正需要做、但真心不想开始做的任务清单？拖延意味着我们花在推迟一项工作上的时间，可能比实际完成它所花的时间还要多。理解我们为什么会拖延，可能有助于我们明白如何停止拖延。
人们拖延的原因各不相同。如果某些任务能让他们联想到过去的创伤经历，有些人会回避这些任务。有时我们不完成某些任务是因为有很多其他事情要忙。如果人们对被要求做某事感到不满，他们可能会推迟，以此来感觉重新获得了一些控制权。拖延的另一个常见原因仅仅是担心做某事会不愉快，或者担心自己做得不够好，无法使自己满意。
这最后一种拖延可能源于我们的思维模式。具有完美主义心态的人可能对任务成功的标准抱有非常严格的想法。再加上对任务失败的焦虑。心理学讲师安妮米克·阿佩吉斯-肖特指出，拖延可能是我们大脑的奖励系统和威胁系统之间斗争的结果。如果失败或不舒适的威胁大于完成任务可能带来的回报，我们很可能会回避它。
认知灵活性可以帮助我们避免拖延。如果我们改变对任务的看法，着手去做就会更容易。如果我们能挑战自己对“成功”的预期，以及完成任务会多么“不舒适”的看法，任务看起来就不会那么有威胁性。将任务分解成小部分也能减少其令人生畏的程度，并在完成每一步时带来成就感。思考是什么触发了你的拖延也可能有所帮助。更好地理解这一点可以帮助你完成任务。

vocabulary.entry: deadline /ˈdedlaɪn/ n. 截止日期，最后期限
vocabulary.example: The deadline for applications is next Friday.
vocabulary.translation: 申请的截止日期是下周五。

vocabulary.entry: procrastination /prəʊˌkræstɪˈneɪʃn/ n. 拖延症，耽搁（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Procrastination is the thief of time.
vocabulary.translation: 拖延是时间的小偷。

vocabulary.entry: put off /ˌpʊt ˈɒf/ phr. v. 推迟，拖延（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: Don't put off until tomorrow what you can do today.
vocabulary.translation: 今日事，今日毕。

vocabulary.entry: procrastinate /prəʊˈkræstɪneɪt/ v. 拖延，耽搁（书面语）
vocabulary.example: He procrastinated so long that he missed the deadline.
vocabulary.translation: 他拖延太久，以至于错过了截止日期。

vocabulary.definition: 与……有关联，涉及（固定表达）
vocabulary.entry: relate to /rɪˈleɪt tu/ phr. v. 与……有关联，涉及（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The two events are closely related to each other.
vocabulary.translation: 这两个事件彼此密切相关。

vocabulary.entry: traumatic /trɔːˈmætɪk/ adj. 创伤的，痛苦的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The accident was a traumatic experience for all involved.
vocabulary.translation: 这次事故对所有相关人员来说都是一次痛苦的经历。

vocabulary.definition: 被淹没的，忙得不可开交的（口语）
vocabulary.entry: swamped /swɒmpt/ adj. 被淹没的，忙得不可开交的（口语）
vocabulary.example: I'm absolutely swamped with work at the moment.
vocabulary.translation: 我眼下工作忙得不可开交。

vocabulary.entry: regain /rɪˈɡeɪn/ v. 重新获得，恢复（书面语）
vocabulary.example: She is trying to regain her confidence after the failure.
vocabulary.translation: 失败后她正努力重新找回自信。

vocabulary.entry: mindset /ˈmaɪndset/ n. 思维模式，心态（书面语）
vocabulary.example: A positive mindset can improve your health.
vocabulary.translation: 积极的心态可以改善你的健康。

vocabulary.entry: perfectionist /pəˈfekʃənɪst/ n. 完美主义者（书面语）
vocabulary.example: As a perfectionist, she spends hours perfecting every detail.
vocabulary.translation: 作为一个完美主义者，她花数小时打磨每一个细节。

vocabulary.entry: rigid /ˈrɪdʒɪd/ adj. 僵化的，固定的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: His views on education are very rigid.
vocabulary.translation: 他对教育的看法非常僵化。

vocabulary.definition: 加上，与……相结合（固定表达）
vocabulary.entry: coupled with /ˈkʌpld wɪð/ phr. 加上，与……相结合（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: His lack of experience, coupled with his poor attitude, led to his dismissal.
vocabulary.translation: 他缺乏经验，加上态度恶劣，导致他被解雇了。

vocabulary.entry: reward /rɪˈwɔːd/ n. 奖励，回报
vocabulary.example: The company offers financial rewards for high performance.
vocabulary.translation: 该公司为表现优异者提供经济奖励。

vocabulary.entry: threat /θret/ n. 威胁
vocabulary.example: Climate change poses a serious threat to coastal cities.
vocabulary.translation: 气候变化对沿海城市构成了严重威胁。

vocabulary.definition: 认知灵活性（心理学专业术语）
vocabulary.entry: cognitive flexibility /ˈkɒɡnətɪv ˌfleksəˈbɪləti/ n. 认知灵活性（心理学专业术语）
vocabulary.example: Cognitive flexibility allows people to adapt to new situations.
vocabulary.translation: 认知灵活性使人们能够适应新情况。

vocabulary.entry: challenge /ˈtʃælɪndʒ/ v. 质疑，挑战
vocabulary.example: The new evidence challenged the traditional theory.
vocabulary.translation: 新证据挑战了传统理论。

vocabulary.entry: expectation /ˌekspekˈteɪʃn/ n. 期望，预期（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The sales figures exceeded our expectations.
vocabulary.translation: 销售数字超出了我们的预期。

vocabulary.entry: break down /ˌbreɪk ˈdaʊn/ phr. v. 分解，拆解（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The problem can be broken down into smaller parts.
vocabulary.translation: 这个问题可以分解成更小的部分。

vocabulary.entry: component /kəmˈpəʊnənt/ n. 组成部分，部件（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The engine has many different components.
vocabulary.translation: 发动机有许多不同的部件。

vocabulary.definition: 令人畏惧的，使人气馁的（书面语）
vocabulary.entry: daunting /ˈdɔːntɪŋ/ adj. 令人畏惧的，使人气馁的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The task seemed daunting at first, but we managed it.
vocabulary.translation: 这项任务起初看起来很艰巨，但我们设法完成了。

vocabulary.entry: achievement /əˈtʃiːvmənt/ n. 成就，成绩（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Winning the award was a great achievement.
vocabulary.translation: 赢得这个奖项是一项巨大的成就。

vocabulary.entry: trigger /ˈtrɪɡə(r)/ v. 触发，引发（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Certain foods can trigger a migraine headache.
vocabulary.translation: 某些食物可能引发偏头痛。

vocabulary.definition: 完成事情，做事有效率（固定表达）
vocabulary.entry: get things done /ˌɡet θɪŋz ˈdʌn/ phr. 完成事情，做事有效率（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: I need to focus and get things done today.
vocabulary.translation: 我今天需要集中精力把事情做好。
